claims.text: Rainier Avenue South & 25th Avenue South had 1 injury crashes in police records since 2021-10-31: 0 people killed.
These counts are Rainier Avenue South & 25th Avenue South's own: the city's record places 161 of the 165 records within 100 m at another intersection or street, and they are left out.
At the U.S. DOT's values that harm costs about $68,000 a year.
No crash pattern here stands out against the city's worst crash locations (too few crashes to test).

The city's Leading Pedestrian Interval signals: passed the causal gate (pedestrian injury crashes changed -33% (95% interval -52% to -13%) at 371 sites against sites treated later or the citywide trend, and a placebo date shows nothing); a second run of the same design on 366 sites agrees.
Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons would avoid about 0.2 crashes a year (CMF 9024, the record FHWA's fact sheet cites; evidence: the record FHWA cites), worth $65,000 a year.

Lighting would avoid about 0.0 crashes a year (CMF 7774, the only eligible record; evidence: only if a site check confirms it), worth $5,000 a year; check on site: the corner has no street lighting now.
The Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is responsible for 25th Avenue South, Rainier Avenue South, South Bayview Street (no route reference, so presumed a city street).
A request letter to the Seattle Department of Transportation (SDOT) is ready to draft from these facts.
